skill.name: markitdown
skill.description: Convert files and office documents to Markdown, including PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, images, audio, HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, ZIP, YouTube URLs, and EPUB files.
skill.summary: Convert documents, media, and structured data into Markdown for AI workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation examples, placeholders, Markdown fences, or expected conversion output writes. Confirmed risks are privileged sudo installation commands, persistent shell-profile API key setup, one optional OpenRouter runtime endpoint, and an unrelated default diagram-generation workflow.

remediation.issue: User-facing setup includes sudo package installation commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before any sudo command and offer non-privileged or package-manager-specific alternatives where possible.

remediation.issue: API key setup examples append credentials to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend a secret manager, session-only environment variables, or project-local ignored env files instead of persistent shell profile writes.

remediation.issue: The AI conversion script can send document content to OpenRouter.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy warning before AI-enhanced conversion and document a local-only conversion path.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs default use of an unrelated scientific schematic generator.
remediation.suggestion: Remove default cross-skill generation behavior or require an explicit user request before using external diagram tools.

content.value_statement: Mixed file formats make document review slow. This skill converts common files into clean Markdown for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Converts PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, images, audio, HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, ZIP, YouTube URLs, and EPUB files to Markdown.
Shows command line and Python API usage for single files, streams, and batch conversion.
Provides optional OpenRouter image descriptions for presentations and image-heavy documents.
Includes scripts for AI-assisted conversion and scientific literature batch processing.
Documents optional dependencies for OCR, audio transcription, YouTube transcription, and Azure Document Intelligence.
Explains troubleshooting steps for missing packages, OCR setup, and API key configuration.
limitations: Requires MarkItDown and optional format dependencies to be installed before use.
AI image descriptions can send document content to OpenRouter or another configured model provider.
OCR and audio transcription quality depend on source quality and installed native tools.
Example scripts write output files and can overwrite user-selected paths.

best_practices: Use a virtual environment and install only the MarkItDown extras required for your file types.
Review converted Markdown before using it for legal, medical, or financial decisions.
Use environment variables or a secret manager for API keys, and avoid committing generated outputs with sensitive content.
anti_patterns: Do not send confidential documents to OpenRouter, Azure, or YouTube workflows without approval.
Do not run sudo installation commands automatically from an agent session.
Do not overwrite source folders with generated Markdown unless backups exist.

faq.question: What does this skill convert?
faq.answer: It converts common office files, PDFs, images, audio, web formats, structured data, archives, and EPUB files into Markdown.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Basic local conversion can work offline, but OpenRouter, Azure Document Intelligence, and YouTube transcription need network access.

faq.question: Can it describe images in documents?
faq.answer: Yes. The optional OpenRouter workflow can add AI-generated image descriptions when a supported vision model is configured.

faq.question: Is it safe for confidential documents?
faq.answer: Use local conversion for confidential files. Do not enable external AI or cloud services unless your policy allows it.

faq.question: Can it process many files at once?
faq.answer: Yes. The included examples and scripts show batch conversion and literature review indexing workflows.

faq.question: What should I install first?
faq.answer: Install MarkItDown in a virtual environment, then add only the optional dependencies needed for your formats.
